title: Lenticular
description: A lenticular picture: views cut into interleaved strips under a barrier grid, flipping as the pointer moves or the phone tilts.

props.name: images
props.description: The views in tilt order (upstream uses three). The smallest size wins; larger ones are center-cropped.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Height of a row of strips in image pixels.

props.name: rowOffset
props.description: Offset of every other row in image pixels.

props.name: maxAngle
props.description: Phone tilt (degrees either way) that sweeps every view.

props.name: track
props.description: What moves the views: the pointer across the window (upstream), across the picture, or nothing.

props.name: tilt
props.description: Follow the device tilt on touch devices (shows a Tilt to play button where permission is needed).

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Called when the pointer, tilt or keys move the sweep.

a11y: A slider (role="slider") named by aria-label, with the visible view as aria-valuetext ("View 2 of 3"). Arrow keys step one view, Home and End jump to the ends; the arrows follow the physical pointer direction in right-to-left pages too.
Reduced motion: pointer and tilt tracking are off and the picture holds still; the keys still change the view.
Before the strips are drawn, or if an image fails to load, the first view shows as a plain image.
usage: <Lenticular images={["/a.png", "/b.png", "/c.png"]} aria-label="A card that changes as you tilt it" />
docs:
Installed `Lenticular` in `components/ui/`, plus the `render-loop` helper in `lib/` and `useReducedMotion` in `hooks/`. Render `<Lenticular images={["/a.png", "/b.png", "/c.png"]} aria-label="..." />` with views of the same size.

The canvases keep the images' pixel size and scale down to fit (`max-w-full`, `max-h-svh`); cap the height with `className="max-h-80"`. The barrier color is `--lenticular-grid` (black). On iPhone a "Tilt to play" button asks for motion permission.
